brief.indication: HFrEF (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction), NYHA class II-IV
brief.business_goal: Grow quarterly prescription volume 15% QoQ over 4 quarters by moving cardiologists and consultant physicians from late/second-line use to guideline-consistent early initiation.
hcp_segments: Consultant physicians with high HF caseload (tier-2/3)
brand_evidence: PARADIGM-HF style pivotal RCT: significant reduction in CV death and HF hospitalisation vs enalapril
Local real-world evidence study (n≈1,200) showing tolerability in Indian patients
Post-hoc analyses in elderly and diabetic subgroups
existing_evidence: Independent meta-analyses supporting ARNI class benefit in HFrEF
Registry data on Indian HF epidemiology (younger onset vs Western cohorts)
evolving_evidence: Emerging data on early in-hospital initiation post-decompensation
Ongoing local health-economics study (readmission cost offset)
guidelines: ESC heart failure guidelines (Class I recommendation for ARNI in HFrEF)
CSI (Cardiological Society of India) position statements
hcp_insights: Advisory board (n=12 cardiologists) - most agree with early initiation in principle but start on ACEi/ARB "to stabilise first"
Field notes - tier-2 physicians cite monthly drug cost as the top reason for not switching

KOLs want local RWE and Indian patient data before advocating publicly
competitors: Generic ACE inhibitors / ARBs (habit + low cost)
SGLT2 inhibitors competing for "next pillar added" mindshare
access_and_cost: Largely out-of-pocket market; monthly cost 8-10x generic ARB
Patient assistance program exists but is under-used by prescribers
constraints: Full compliance with UCPMP; no inducements; MLR review on all materials

doctrine.name: The First-Touch Doctrine
doctrine.thesis: The enemy of CardioShield is not the comparator molecule. It is the ritual of delay — the 'stabilise first' habit that postpones guideline therapy past the only moment that reliably converts.
doctrine.bet: Every eligible first encounter is the guideline encounter.
doctrine.whyNovel: Most launch decks sell a better drug. This doctrine retires a clinical habit. Evidence is used as permission to act now, not as a brochure of superiority.

slides.narrative: Theme: Every eligible first encounter is the guideline encounter.
bullets: Pillar 1 — Permission now: the first eligible encounter is the guideline encounter.
Pillar 2 — Practical confidence: monitoring and cost have a protocol, not a shrug.
Pillar 3 — Peer cover: someone like you already starts here.

callout.label: MLR
callout.text: Every pillar must carry a named evidence row. No pillar ships without a grade and a caveat.

slides.title: Five moves that retire the ritual
slides.narrative: Ideas are cheap. Interventions have an owner, a COM-B lever, a segment, and a kill-criterion.
bullets: First-Touch Protocol — A hospital-to-clinic initiation bundle so CardioShield is started at the first eligible encounter.
Affordability Confidence Kit — A field-legal script, PAP mechanics, and HE one-pager that lets the HCP stay on the patient's side.
Myth-Reset Asset — One wrong belief, one local number, one peer voice. Unlearning, not a lecture.
Peer Cascade — Metro KOLs author the protocol; tier-2 peers demonstrate it. Cover travels down, not out as a TV ad.
Habit-Lock CRM — The second prescription is designed, not hoped for. Prompts, feedback, peer norms.

slides.title: Impact against friction — the Q1 mix is not the year mix
slides.narrative: Q1 buys proof of mechanism: one hospital pathway, one cost kit, one myth-reset asset. Q2–Q4 scale what moved a driver.

slides.title: A single HCP should feel a designed sequence, not a spray
slides.narrative: Pre-launch builds peer cover. Launch installs the first-touch protocol. Adoption locks the habit. Beyond the campaign, the pathway stays.

interventions.name: First-Touch Protocol

interventions.mlr: Protocol language must match label and local code. No start-all implication.
interventions.kill: If discharge initiation rate is unchanged at week 8 in the pilot site.

interventions.name: Affordability Confidence Kit
interventions.promise: A field-legal script, PAP mechanics, and HE one-pager that lets the HCP stay on the patient's side.
interventions.segment: Tier-2 consultants and high OOP caseloads
interventions.mlr: No price promises. Assistance, not inducement.
interventions.kill: If PAP mention rate rises but initiation does not.

interventions.name: Myth-Reset Asset
interventions.promise: One wrong belief, one local number, one peer voice. Unlearning, not a lecture.
interventions.mlr: Comparative safety claims need the source grade on-slide.
interventions.kill: If unaided myth prevalence does not drop in the next insight wave.

interventions.name: Peer Cascade
interventions.promise: Metro KOLs author the protocol; tier-2 peers demonstrate it. Cover travels down, not out as a TV ad.
interventions.kill: If cascade stops at the same five names by Q2.

interventions.name: Habit-Lock CRM
interventions.promise: The second prescription is designed, not hoped for. Prompts, feedback, peer norms.
interventions.mlr: CRM content is promotional and goes through MLR.
interventions.kill: If repeat rate among trialists is flat vs control geographies.
